listen.script: Boy: What did you think of the match last night? Girl: To be honest, I found it a bit boring. Nobody scored until the last minute. But the way I see it, the better team won.
listen.q: What was the girl's opinion of the match?
options: It was exciting from the start.
It was boring, but the better team won.

listen.script: Woman: I think we should go to the beach this weekend. Man: I see your point, but it's going to be very hot. Why don't we go to the museum instead and visit the beach in winter?
options: Going to the beach this weekend.
Going to the museum now and the beach later.

listen.script: Teacher: You look stressed out, Saad. Boy: I've got three exams next week, and I'm falling behind in science. Teacher: If I were you, I'd make a timetable and ask your science teacher for extra help.
options: Make a timetable and ask for help.

listen.script: Girl: Excuse me, I left my bag behind. It's a small green bag which has a pattern of yellow flowers. I think I left it in the café where I had lunch, near the bookshop.
listen.q: What does the girl's bag look like?
options: Big and yellow, with green stars.
Small and green, with yellow flowers.
Small and brown, made of leather.

read.passage: Last month, students at a school in Dammam had a class debate. The question was: 'Should students be allowed to use phones at break time?' Fahad was convinced that phones are useful. He said, 'In my opinion, we can use them to call our parents or check our homework.' His classmate Nawaf didn't agree. 'I see your point,' he said, 'but if everyone looks at a phone, nobody will play or talk.' In the end, the teacher gave some advice: 'If I were you, I'd keep phones in your bags at break and use them only after school.' Most students said that the idea made sense, so the class came to an agreement.

qs.q: Why does Fahad think phones are useful?
options: Students can call their parents or check homework.
Students won't play or talk at break.
Phones will break in the playground.

qs.q: What did the class decide in the end?
options: To keep phones in bags at break and use them after school.

qs.q: How did Nawaf disagree with Fahad?
options: He politely accepted Fahad's idea first and then gave his own.
